# Git Reality Delta

The Awtsmoos lets the fetched horizon correct the map before release may rise;
Awtsmoos.com follows the remote main that actually exists, not an earlier snapshot wearing yesterday's guise.

## Correction

The first scan briefly showed local `main` and `origin/main` at different SHAs. A subsequent ancestry read proved the local branch had no unique commits and the remote had the newer lineage. During source review, other release activity continued and the origin-only log became empty, proving the shared main horizon was moving in real time.

Therefore the release does not trust the earlier SHA. It performs a new `git fetch origin main` immediately before constructing its isolated worktree, uses that exact `origin/main` SHA as the base, and copies only the audited SEO working-tree files into the isolated vessel.
